Purpose This manual defines the preventive maintenance (PM) activities, operating parameters and common alarms for the TX-200 CNC turning centres (machines CNC-04 to CNC-09) used on the shaft machining line. 2. Never open the electrical cabinet or hydraulic circuit on a running or energised machine. 3. Preventive Maintenance Schedule Frequency Activity Done by Daily (start of shift) Check hydraulic pressure, coolant level, way lube level, air pressure; clean chips from slideways Operator Weekly Check coolant concentration; clean coolant tank filter; check chuck jaw wear Operator Monthly Check spindle runout; inspect hydraulic hoses for leaks or cracks; clean electrical cabinet fan filter Maintenance technician Quarterly Replace hydraulic return filter; check turret alignme

hoses for leaks or cracks; clean electrical cabinet fan filter Maintenance technician Quarterly Replace hydraulic return filter; check turret alignment; check backlash on X and Z axes Maintenance technician Yearly Replace hydraulic oil (ISO VG 46); full geometric accuracy check; replace coolant completely Maintenance engineer 5. Chuck Mounting Bolt Torque When re-mounting the chuck after maintenance, tighten the mounting bolts in a criss-cross sequence to 110 Nm using a calibrated torque wrench. 6. Common Alarms Alarm Meaning Operator action AL-101 Hydraulic pressure low Stop cycle. Check oil level and pressure gauge. Call maintenance if pressure stays below 3.5 MPa.

AL-210 Chuck clamp not confirmed Do not start cycle. Check chuck pressure and part seating. Call maintenance if repeated. AL-305 Spindle overload Stop cycle. Check tool wear and cutting parameters. Inform shift supervisor. AL-412 Coolant level low Top up coolant mixed to 6 - 8 % concentration. 7. Replacing a Hydraulic Hose 1. Isolate the machine as per SAF-SOP-003, including releasing stored hydraulic pressure. 2. Confirm the panel pressur

. 7. Replacing a Hydraulic Hose 1. Isolate the machine as per SAF-SOP-003, including releasing stored hydraulic pressure. 2. Confirm the panel pressure gauge reads zero before loosening any fitting. 3. Place a drip tray under the hose and loosen the fittings slowly. 4. Fit a new hose of the same rating and tighten fittings. 5. Remove locks as per SAF-SOP-003, start the hydraulic unit and confirm pressure returns to 3.5 - 4.0 MPa with no leaks.

Purpose This procedure describes how incoming raw materials and bought-out components are inspected at the receiving area before they are released to stores and production. 2. Scope Applies to all steel bar stock, castings, forgings and bought-out components received at the Hosur plant. 3. Responsibilities • Stores Executive: receives m

Responsibilities • Stores Executive: receives material, checks quantity against the delivery challan and informs QC. • QC Inspector: carries out sampling, visual and dimensional inspection, and records results. • QC Supervisor: approves acceptance or rejection of the lot. 4. Procedure 1. Stores Executive places the received lot in the Incoming Inspection Area and raises an inspection request. 2. QC Inspector collects the purchase order, drawing and supplier test certificate (if available). 3. Draw 5 samples at random from every lot, irrespective of lot size. 4. Perform visual inspection for

g and supplier test certificate (if available). 3. Draw 5 samples at random from every lot, irrespective of lot size. 4. Perform visual inspection for rust, dents, cracks and burrs. 5. Perform dimensional inspection on all critical dimensions using a vernier caliper. 6. If all 5 samples are within specification, the lot is accepted. Scope Applies to all steel bar stock, castings, forgings and bought-out components received at the Hosur plant, including machined BH-220 bearing housings received from sub-contractors. 3. Responsibilities • Stores Executive: receives material, checks quantity against the delivery challan and raises the inspection request in the QMS app. • QC Inspector: carries out sampling, visual and dimensional inspection, and records results in the QMS app. • Shift QC Supervisor: approves acceptance, rejection or hold of the lot. • Supplier Quality Engineer (SQE): handles supplier communication for rejected or held lots. 4. Sampling Plan Defects are classified as follows: • Critical: a defect that can cause a safety risk or failure of the part, e.g. crack, wrong material grade, or a dimension out of tolerance on a characteristic marked Critical. • Major: a defect that affects fit or function but is not critical, e.g. deep dent, damaged thread, or a dimension out of tolerance on a characteristic marked Major. • Minor: a cosmetic defect that does not affect fit or function, e.g. light surface marks or light surface rust that can be removed by cleaning. SAF-SOP-003 | Rev 05 | Uncontrolled copy when printed. Refer to QMS for the latest version. Page 1 Kaveri Precision Components Pvt. Ltd. - Hosur Plant Lockout / Tagout (LOTO) - Safety Procedure Document No. SAF-SOP-003 Revision 05 Effective Date 12-Feb-2026 Page See footer Prepared By J. Fathima, Safety Officer Approved By A. Krishnan, Plant Head 1. Purpose To protect people from the unexpected start-up of machines or release of stored energy (electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic, mechanical) during maintenance, cleaning, setting or repair. 2. Scope Applies to all employees and contract workers at the Hosur plant who maintain, clean or repair machines, including CNC turning centres, presses and

e Applies to all employees and contract workers at the Hosur plant who maintain, clean or repair machines, including CNC turning centres, presses and compressors. 3. Definitions • Authorised person: a trained employee who applies their own personal lock and tag to isolate energy. • Affected person: an operator or employee who works in the area but does not perform the isolation. • Zero energy state: the condition where all energy sources are isolated and stored energy is released, so that the machine cannot move or release energy. 4. Lockout Procedure 1. Inform all affected persons that the machine is being shut down for maintenance. 2. Stop the machine using the normal stop sequence. 3. Iso

ocedure 1. Inform all affected persons that the machine is being shut down for maintenance. 2. Stop the machine using the normal stop sequence. 3. Isolate all energy sources: main electrical isolator, compressed air valve, and hydraulic power unit. 4. Apply your personal red lock and danger tag to each isolation point. Each authorised person working on the machine applies their own lock. Use a multi-lock hasp when more than one person is involved. 5. Release stored energy: bleed hydraulic pressure and accumulators until the gauge reads zero, vent compressed air to 0 bar, and block any parts that can fall under gravity. 6. Verify zero energy: try to start the machine from the control panel an

nt compressed air to 0 bar, and block any parts that can fall under gravity. 6. Verify zero energy: try to start the machine from the control panel and confirm it does not start. Confirm all pressure gauges read zero. Return controls to OFF. 5. Removing Locks 1. Check that tools and materials are removed and guards are refitted. 2. Confirm all persons are clear of the machine. 3. Each authorised person removes only their own lock. Nobody may remove another person's lock. 4. Inform affected persons that the machine is being restarted. 6. Removal of a Lock When the Owner Is Absent If an authorised person has left the plant without removing their lock, the lock may be removed only through this

of a Lock When the Owner Is Absent If an authorised person has left the plant without removing their lock, the lock may be removed only through this procedure: 1. The Shift Supervisor makes every reasonable effort to contact the lock owner by phone. 2. If the owner cannot be reached, the Production Manager and the Safety Officer must both authorise removal. 3. The machine is physically inspected to confirm it is safe to re-energise.

SAF-SOP-003 | Rev 05 | Uncontrolled copy when printed. Refer to QMS for the latest version. Page 2 4. The removal is recorded on form SF-12 Lock Removal Record. 5. The lock owner must be informed before they resume work on their next shift. 7. Training and Audits • All authorised persons must complete LOTO training before applying locks, with refresher training every 12 months. • The Safety Officer audits LOTO practice on each shift at least once a month. • Violation of this procedure is treated as a serious safety breach.
